name: Osaka
tagline: Come hungry. Stay for the lights.
summary: A food-first city with neon waterways and lively shopping streets. Pair the compact southern districts, then give the bay or theme park a separate day.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are comfortable. Summer is hot and humid; major holidays bring theme-park crowds.
arrival: Kansai Airport has rail to Namba and the wider region. Shinkansen trains arrive at Shin-Osaka, not central Osaka Station.
gettingAround: Use metro and regional rail. Namba, Dotonbori, Kuromon and Doguyasuji can be combined on foot.
cashTip: Keep yen for street snacks and smaller stores; many larger venues accept cards.
foodTip: Try takoyaki, okonomiyaki and kushikatsu. Let freshly cooked fillings cool before eating.
buyTip: Kitchen tools in Doguyasuji, everyday shopping in Shinsaibashi and hobby goods in Nipponbashi.
baseArea: Namba for food and evenings; Umeda for regional rail connections.

connections.note: Choose JR, Hankyu or Keihan based on the neighborhoods; allow station walks.
Depart Shin-Osaka; reserve for busy dates and check luggage rules.

reviewSummary: Dotonbori, Kaiyukan and Osaka Castle appear among the retrieved review platform’s leading attractions. The castle is a museum inside a reconstructed keep; choose it for exhibits as well as the exterior.
